title: LIGHTHOUSE identifies riboflavin 5′-monophosphate as a PPAT inhibitor
summary: LIGHTHOUSE, a deep-learning model using protein sequence and chemical representations, nominated riboflavin 5′-monophosphate as an inhibitor of PPAT, a target without reported inhibitors in the paper. A biochemical assay measured PPAT inhibition with an IC50 of 7.5 μM, close to the model’s predicted range; the same study also tested predicted antiviral compounds in cell models.

evidence.tested: LIGHTHOUSE, a deep-learning model using protein sequence and chemical representations, nominated riboflavin 5′-monophosphate as an inhibitor of PPAT, a target without reported inhibitors in the paper.
evidence.unknown: The result is an in-vitro enzyme assay, not a validated anticancer treatment. The authors note LIGHTHOUSE can produce false positives; COVID-19 results were also cell-based and had no clinical evidence.
evidence.ai_role: The model scored protein–compound relationships without requiring a 3D target structure and prioritized the compound from >333,000 candidates for experimental follow-up. The authors assayed PPAT activity and confirmed inhibition in vitro.
